title: Build gradually at a justified effort on the retained route
stage_label: Separate instructional session · Week 2, Day 3 · individually authored
status_note: Written athletic lesson independently reviewed. Current canonical approval, actual facility/athlete readiness and precise separate tumbling remain unverified.
brief: Connect actually repeatable easy running to one modest effort decision on the same35m corridor. Retain the easy task when progression is not justified. Keep the counted whole-route walk, comfortable preparation and five familiar strength roles. The new variable is the chosen running effort; route, opportunity count and strength complexity are held or deliberately reduced.
quality_target: Smooth buildup at the selected comfortable effort, relaxed rhythm through the running finish, controlled gradual slowing in the verified runoff and recovered return. Record actual route, effort, cue needs and response. A planned4/10 cue, short start or walking result does not establish higher-speed competence.
continuity: Actual OR04 running/route and actual OR07 or other recent exposure → OR08 modest effort decision or hold on the retained route with compatible strength → OR12 retains actual output/route while recovery responsibility changes; OR16 observes the same actual task.
audience: Ages12–14 are the reference, not beginners. Every age has explicit booking/D-L/route doses and independent competence overrides. Five offered days are optional attendance opportunities. Existing qualified athletes may bypass unnecessary instruction into an independently eligible main-entry branch; newcomers use actual component instruction rather than age or visit-count assumptions.
readiness: Before the first modest increase, check actual easy-run repeatability, route conduct and gradual slowing. To retain modest work, use actual repeatable same-route2→4/4 and current response without demanding an older easy-run record. Check that the retained runoff fits the proposed actual demand; if uncertain, retain easy intent or defer instead of a screening run. P2 and E0 observe narrower tasks. Review actual OR06 flight/hinge and OR07 stopping/stance/unloading or equivalent recent sport/tumbling response. Preserve most recent reduced counts and unloaded hip work. Symptoms, restrictions, distress or unsafe traffic stop the affected task.
equipment_space:
UNVERIFIED MODEL:15 separate3×3m preparation bays, peripheral coach access, three protected straight35m corridors at2m planning width each and three separate one-way outside returns. Long route remains0–10m build,10–20m rhythm,20–35m gradual runoff. The short route remains0–5m target/5–15m runout; it is a different objective, never simulated maximal velocity. P2 uses the short geometry even when E0/E1 use the long route. Pre-position both finish-marker sets, clearly distinguish the active choice before release and do not move markers while any athlete uses that lane. Inspect the actual runoff for the selected demand; these dimensions are not universal safe distances.

Each lane has its own return and rear waiting line behind its start, with no shared merge, cross-lane rejoin or crossing of the next-athlete feed. Turns, rejoin and any ordinary staging belong inside the prescribed return/setup allowance. Inspect full actual path lengths and unforced walking time; no return metres are inferred from the timer. Stationary tasks stay in personal bays outside all active/return/staging paths and directly visible from the assigned coach’s viewing position. Any transfer back after a traveling P2 occurs inside main-relative0–120s setup. If the full route and stationary bay cannot be observed from the assigned safe position, omit/defer that combination under this schedule.

Five fitting knee/hip bays, five high stable press supports, five row benches and suitable single row DBs, five floor mats, and five leg supports or verified suspension anchors for selected replacements. Familiar two-DB hip work additionally needs five individually fitting elevated pickup/parking stations and TEN simultaneously suitable DBs in the actual retained pairs/loads. These are not ten interchangeable arbitrary weights. The rows may reuse suitable DBs only after all hip work is parked/cleared, within later setup. Every apparatus position, load pair, traction, spacing, body clearance and coach sightline remains unverified.
coaching_flow:
P1 uses three observed groups of five in personal bays. P2 and E0 use three eligible slow-travel athletes per wave, one per lane, with two coaches dividing observation1/2 from actual useful viewing positions. Stationary athletes occupy the same reserved slot in their visible personal bay, never an uncounted transfer to a lane. Unresolved conduct or a need for continuous escort means individually adapt/omit/defer, not an unseen third athlete.

E1 keeps15 numbered releases at30s intervals, cyclingA/B/C lanes. Coach1 takes even zero-based indices and Coach2 odd, with the same assignment each round. Each coach gets60s between assigned starts and at least15s after the longest45s active walking observation. Coaches observe from verified positions, not by shadowing35m and rushing back. Each return/queue must remain visible and use already understood conduct; if simultaneous observation and traffic cannot be managed, delay/omit rather than claim this model was delivered. A stationary E1 uses its10s in the assigned bay/slot, without a lane start or return.

Five-person strength groups require direct two-coach views, each observing two or three familiar athletes. The familiar DB option is permitted only for independently controlled retained handling/lifting at the actual pair/load/count, not first implement instruction. All five have fitting stations and pairs ready before that wave. Stop for unsuitable supervision or handling. Reserve20s between hip waves for the coaches to check/prepare the next retained pairs after all implements are parked and the group clears; no reset occurs while those coaches are observing active lifts. Choose a compatible unloaded set or defer before pickup if the model does not fit.
clock: Explosiveness / retained route and running-intent decision
time_rules: All times are earliest planning releases and upper action/return allowances, not gait requirements. Keep actual instruction, travel, runoff, exit, return turns/rejoin, staging, water and strength transitions inside the booked clock. Pre-position route markers; no active-gap relocation. A fault consumes an attempt; record partial work and use only an independently eligible easier choice in a remaining listed opportunity or defer. No extra screening/correction repetition or repayment work. A longer actual action/return delays subsequent releases and removes later uncompleted work.
preparation_note: Keep the complete reviewed instructional base and concluding hinge/squat checks. Exactly two targets use40s P1 basic rhythm and140s P2 retained short initiation/runout or its independently selected smaller task. The outline’s full-route progressive rehearsal is explicitly reconciled: one full-route walk is E0, and the first purposeful intent is E1 counted work. P2 does not run the full35m corridor or use the new4/10 cue.

exercises.name: Retain the comfortable basic rhythm
exercises.mapping: BASIC-MARCH-TEACH; quiet-standing alternative is separately mapped
exercises.set_purpose: One four-step rehearsal retains comfortable upright organization and opposite arm/leg timing while the later run receives the effort decision. The quiet-standing replacement observes only its own simpler participation.
exercises.execution: Stay in the assigned personal bay. Alternate four comfortable marching steps in place, two each side, at2s per step; settle2s. Keep one foot supported throughout and use relaxed opposite arm/leg motion. No forward travel or forced high knee is added.
exercises.cues: Comfortable steps; stand comfortably tall; opposite arm and leg; settle.
exercises.errors: Calling the in-place task exact traveling A-March, introducing flight, forcing thigh height, leaning back or adding repetitions while other groups work.
exercises.rationale: The same basic in-place pattern is sufficient for this focused preparation observation. Traveling A-March, a higher knee target or skipping would introduce another change without establishing the full-route running prerequisite.
exercises.metadata: Method: counted stationary rhythm rehearsal. Tenets: Coordination/Body Control/Balance. Pattern: alternating no-flight support. Equipment: personal bay.

standard_D.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation
standard_D.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
standard_D.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

exercises.competency: Comfortable ordinary walking/support exchange and stop-cue participation must be present. Missing or unsuitable marching selects the explicit quiet-standing task, not forced supported marching. All three ages retain this small dose; experienced athletes receive a concise cue rather than added height/flight.
exercises.progression: Retain four individual steps, two each side,2s each plus2s settle. P1 recovery is20s before repeating this short pattern. Do not increase height, travel, flight or count because effort may change later.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR04/basic preparation rhythm and recent coordination → one retained P1 observation → OR08 main running choice → OR12 retains the actual pattern while recovery responsibility is taught.

exercises.name: Retain a short start/runout or eligible preparation alternative
exercises.mapping: ACC-STATIC low-intent contextual use, or WALK-CORRIDOR-TEACH; no-travel adaptations separately declared
exercises.set_purpose: One counted short rehearsal preserves release, gradual initiation and use of a protected finish/runout. It supplies no full35m running or higher-intent result. A walking/marching/standing choice rehearses only its own narrower task.
exercises.execution: The qualified low-intent route starts still in a comfortable bilateral standing stance, uses a smooth5m start, then slows gradually through10m protected runout and exits into its dedicated return. Unknown running readiness uses an ordinary15m corridor walk. Each route has its own active/return envelope below; no athlete walks the full35m route here. The main E0 task owns that longer physical orientation.
exercises.cues: Wait for release; smooth start; pass the finish; use the runout; walk back outside.
exercises.errors: Max effort from the first step, changing to a moving or three-point entry, stopping sharply at5m, entering the forward lane on return or adding a second rehearsal after a fault.
exercises.rationale: Retain the known15m preparation task inside140s. Full-route walking remains E0; the first modest intent change is counted E1. This is an explicit preparation amendment to the outline, not a claim that a short start rehearses the whole long route.
exercises.metadata: Method: single observed route rehearsal. Tenets: Coordination/Explosiveness/Body Control as eligible. Bodyweight; marked15m protected route and separate return.

exercises.competency: Select P2 independently of E1. Short start requires actual comfortable standing initiation, easy contacts and gradual runout/conduct. Short walking needs its own safe route and walking ability; stationary marching needs comfortable support exchange; standing needs comfortable independent standing. An athlete with independently known long-running competence may take a smaller P2 without losing or gaining that evidence. Neither a P2 choice nor its completion supplies main-run permission.
exercises.progression: Keep actual standing start,5m easy2→3/10 initiation and10m gradual runout. No4/10 intent is inserted in preparation. All ages get one eligible P2 attempt with60s recovery, or the explicit narrower replacement; a fault consumes the opportunity.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR04 short preparation or direct equivalent → one retained short/position task → counted E0 route observation and independently eligible E1 intent choice → OR12 retains the actually selected route.

exercises.name: Confirm the complete selected corridor with one counted walk
exercises.mapping: WALK-CORRIDOR-TEACH — ordinary route orientation, not a braking or speed test
exercises.set_purpose: One actual route walk confirms today’s markers, ordinary exit and outside return before the run decision. It preserves the prior low-demand observation without adding a running screen or rewarding attendance with a speed increase.
exercises.execution: On the long route, walk0–10m build area,10–20m intended upright area and20–35m protected runoff, identify their markers in the coach’s allotted pause, then exit and walk back by the dedicated one-way return. On a short route, walk0–5m target and5–15m runout. Do not add a two-second athletic stick, turn-and-go or measured braking task. No-travel selection uses a quiet standing orientation while the coach explains the diagram; actual corridor travel remains unobserved.
exercises.cues: Name the finish; show the runoff; find the outside return; wait for the next release.
exercises.errors: Treating verbal knowledge as completed running, stopping at the running finish instead of using the remaining corridor, taking the forward lane back or leaving this walk out of total workload.
exercises.rationale: The familiar route still needs today’s traffic/marker observation. Keep this walk counted in the main clock; it observes walking and conduct while prior actual running and current readiness determine E1.
exercises.metadata: Method: counted route walkthrough, full recovery. Tenets: Coordination/Body Control. Walking distance is separate from later running targets.

exercises.competency: Comfortable independent walking, simple release/stop communication and safe corridor/return are required. The first listed walk is the route observation, not an assumed completed prerequisite. If traffic understanding is incomplete, continue only an eligible walking or stationary teaching route. A long corridor that does not fit is a facility limitation, not an athlete failure.
exercises.progression: Retain one whole35m long or15m short walk with its complete return; a stationary route instead observes its diagram in a personal bay. Do not add a second walk or practice run to obtain a pass.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR04 route and current P2 selection → one counted E0 walking/standing observation → E1 only with its separate actual running evidence → OR12 retains the actual route while athlete recovery responsibility changes.

exercises.name: Choose a modest running-intent increase or retain the easy run
exercises.mapping: EASY-BUILD-RUN-TEACH; independently eligible short acceleration/walking/stationary alternatives
exercises.set_purpose: Each listed run practices smooth buildup and relaxed rhythm at one selected effort on the retained route. The purposeful branch teaches its first2→4/4 attempt only after repeatable prior2→3/3 running and suitable slowing. The easy branch retains or teaches the existing easy task. Two standard D or one compressed D opportunities, before a smaller cap, share that same purpose; there is no faster second-round target.
exercises.execution: From still comfortable bilateral standing, use the same0–10m build,10–20m rhythm and20–35m gradual runoff. Purposeful branch: smoothly rise from about2/10 toward4/10 and retain relaxed4/10 through the rhythm zone. Easy branch: rise2→3 and retain3. Natural reciprocal arms and self-selected comfortable steps; no forced upright posture at the start, reaching for stride length, all-out intent or race. Gradually slow through the protected runoff and exit before returning outside. Markers are task/space boundaries, not forced stopping deadlines. If slowing, traffic or coordination is unsuitable, end the affected run safely and record partial travel; use only an independently eligible easier choice in a remaining listed opportunity or defer. No extra trial earns a pass.
exercises.cues: Smooth build. Keep the chosen effort comfortable and relaxed. Run through the finish. Ease down. Return outside and recover.
exercises.errors: Running a timed fly or maximal second half; making estimated segment seconds into pace targets; forcing a stop at35m; changing route/count/strength load while calling it intent alone; using short preparation or a walk as proof of repeatable long running; adding a correction attempt.
exercises.rationale: The actual easy-run anchor provides a comparison for a modest effort decision. Keep route, start, count and full recovery so the observation concerns effort/rhythm/slowing. An already faster qualified athlete does not need a novice reset: use the appropriate separately qualified main-entry route when the on-ramp’s lower-demand lesson is unnecessary. This session does not import the archived maximal stride-out or a flying-sprint profile.
exercises.metadata: Method: recovered progressive-intent practice, or deliberate hold/instruction. Tenets: Speed, Explosiveness, Coordination and Body Control according to the actual route. Movement intelligence appears in effort/route awareness; resilience in controlled slowing and suitable recovery. No maximal-velocity result or guaranteed adaptation is claimed.

standard_D.variant: Progressive Build and Upright Rhythm Run — modest nonmaximal intent context
standard_D.effort_load: Bodyweight. From still comfortable standing, build smoothly over0–10m from about2/10 toward4/10, then keep relaxed purposeful4/10 through10–20m. Slow gradually through20–35m. This is a provisional coaching effort cue, not a speed percentage, required pace or maximal/flying sprint.
standard_D.notes: Each set is one whole counted attempt including any fault. Active/exit estimate25s; separate outside walking return40s. These are logistics estimates, not forced cadence. No corrective or assessment repetition is added. Exact steps/contacts and return metres remain actual observations. Retain the actual smaller compatible opportunity count. All25s active phases are planning allowances, not segment targets; earlier clearance leaves quiet time. The full40s outside return includes turning/rejoining. Longer actual action/return delays later releases; omit uncompleted later work instead of forcing pace. Record actual effort, slowing and faults; no extra trial.

exercises.competency: Purposeful running has two explicit entry paths. FIRST modest increase requires actual repeatable easy long-route running at2→3/3, coordinated contacts and gradual slowing. RETAINED modest work requires actual repeatable same-route2→4/4 with controlled slowing, without reconstructing an older3/10 record. Both require suitable current response and verified route/runoff for the selected demand. Record increase versus hold; one emerging attempt or attendance establishes neither repeatability. Prior easy success alone does not prove that15m runoff fits4/10 today; the coach must evaluate the actual athlete and available space before release. No prior successful4/10 attempt is required to teach the first counted one. If that assessment is uncertain, hold easy intent or defer; do not add a screening sprint. Easy-running instruction still requires independently comfortable easy jogging, coordinated contacts, gradual slowing and actual route conduct, but not previous mastery of the whole35m lesson. E0 walking and P2 short work cannot substitute for missing running prerequisites. L does not run. Symptoms, restrictions, unsafe paths, distress or declining control stop the affected work.
exercises.progression: Change only a justified intent cue from actual2→3/3 to2→4/4. Hold the actual start,35m geometry, opportunities, full recovery and familiar strength demands. Main referenceD2standard/1compressed,Lwalking1standard/0compressed; cap1 preserves actual smaller prior opportunities. Never restore a missing run or turn the second round into a faster test. If actual recent intent was already4/10, record a hold, not a new increase; this reference does not prescribe higher output.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR04 easy-run/route evidence plus OR07 or other recent lower-body response → one justified modest effort decision or retained easy/alternate task → OR12 keeps actual output/route while teaching recovery responsibility → OR16 compares the actual retained task without claiming maximal speed.

exercises.name: Retain the familiar bilateral knee pattern
exercises.set_purpose: One familiar bodyweight squat set supplies the knee role without adding a new load or stance task to the running lesson. Keep actual comfortable depth and smaller repetitions; it complements the hip/push/pull/brace roles.
exercises.execution: Use a comfortable bilateral base and owned range. Lower3s, pause gently1s, stand1s. Keep whole-foot pressure and natural breathing. No box or hand support is assumed.
exercises.cues: Whole foot; comfortable squat; pause softly; stand tall.
exercises.errors: Forcing depth, bouncing, holding breath or treating this supporting set as a loading test.
exercises.rationale: Return to the bilateral squat’s own actual record. OR07’s supported split holds are a different task and do not translate into squat repetitions or justify an extra unilateral set.
exercises.metadata: Method: retained observed practice. Tenets: Strength/Body Control. Pattern: bilateral knee. Equipment: none.

exercises.competency: Use the actual comfortable bodyweight squat with controlled lowering, brief pause and standing, as observed in the concluding base check or direct evidence. Unknown history uses one explicitly taught two-repetition set in every age, with the first listed repetition counted as instruction. No extra test or loaded goblet change today.
exercises.progression: One set; D3/4/4 or L2/3/3 across9–11/12–14/15–18 only when compatible with actual recent counts. Explicit1/2/3 ceilings use min(reference,cap). Keep3s lower,1s pause,1s stand,5s setup,60s recovery and at least5 good reps in reserve. The smaller actual dose stays smaller.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR04/05/06 bilateral squat or direct equivalent and recent OR07 stance response → one retained/reduced bilateral set → OR10’s separate squat/load decision uses actual response, not OR08 running progress.

exercises.name: Retain the most recent compatible hip variation and count
exercises.mapping: HINGE-BW; independently familiar TWO-DB RDL alternative retains DB-RDL mechanics
exercises.set_purpose: One supporting hip set retains the most recent compatible pattern and dose. Bodyweight remains bodyweight after actual OR07 unloading. A genuinely familiar currently retained two-DB set can remain loaded if its own handling, supervision and recent-history conditions hold; neither choice adds a new strength progression.
exercises.execution: Default: arms crossed at chest, soft knees, hips back3s and stand1s through owned range,5s setup/exit. Familiar DB alternative: actual retained pair at individually fitting elevated parking positions. Hold one DB in each hand with palms inward and arms long; establish a comfortable tall top start with weights near the thighs. Hinge through the owned comfortable hamstring-limited range, with no floor-touch or forced stretch target;4s controlled pickup, three-second lowering/one-second standing repetitions,4s controlled set-down and2s clear. Soft knees, organized trunk, weights remain close; no wall touch, new reach target or grip/handling test. Record kg per DB, total load and actual parking height/range. First-time pickup/top-start/hinge/set-down instruction is not available in this loaded route.
exercises.cues: Keep the owned setup. Hips back. Stand smoothly. Park both weights under control when using them.
exercises.errors: Restoring old DBs after more recent unloading; assuming a firstOR06 teaching set proves familiar handling; one implement substituted for two; a new load or longer set; rushed handling or an extra trial to choose the route.
exercises.rationale: Preserve a useful hip anchor while effort is considered in the run. Do not search back to an older productive DB record to undo a newer reduction. A familiar loaded athlete who missed OR07 is not assigned fictitious unloading history.
exercises.metadata: Method: retained or reduced supporting hip practice. Tenets: Strength and Body Control. Bodyweight good morning or independently familiar two-dumbbell RDL; exact identity and handling remain distinct.

exercises.competency: Bodyweight requires comfortable owned hinge control; unknown history uses the explicit one×2 unloaded teaching set for every age. Familiar DB is D only and requires actual most-recent compatible loaded hip evidence at the same pair/load/count, independent controlled pickup/top-start/repetitions/set-down and suitable response. A single first-DB instructional set alone supplies no automatic familiar-handling pass. Actual OR07 unloading or a newer low record blocks automatic restoration. Five fitting elevated parking stations, ten simultaneously suitable DBs, separated bays and direct two-coach observation are required for the group loaded option. If unavailable, select a deliberately unloaded compatible set or defer before pickup; a fault after pickup is counted and ends the affected set, without a replacement set.
exercises.progression: One set only. Bodyweight D3/4/4,L2/3/3 at4s each+5s handling,60s rest. Familiar DB D3/4/4 in either booking at4s each+10s complete handling,90s rest and at least5 good reps in reserve; zero loaded sets inL. Explicit1/2/3 repetition ceilings preserve actual smaller counts in either variant. No first loaded setup, extra set or load restoration accompanies a new running-intent lesson.
exercises.continuity: Most recent actual OR06/07 or equivalent hip variant, handling, load, repetitions and response → one compatible retained/reduced set → OR10/15 use actual response and the earlier productive record while preserving more recent reductions.

exercises.name: Retain supported pressing
exercises.set_purpose: One familiar push set retains a complementary full-body quality without changing the running task or adding another strength progression. Use the actual fitting setup and compatible count; the explicit low support level preserves more recent lighter work.
exercises.execution: Use the verified high support with hands secure and feet at their recorded position. Keep an organized body line, lower2s and press1s through an owned range. The first listed rep is the observation.
exercises.cues: Stable hands; one body line; controlled lower; press away.
exercises.errors: Sag/pike, forced depth, unstable surface, uncounted demonstration reps or a lower support assigned solely to older athletes.
exercises.rationale: The push role remains separately coached after knee and hip work. It balances the session without pretending to cause the running-intent change. No superset, extra circuit or finisher is added.
exercises.metadata: Method: retained supported practice. Tenets: Strength/Body Control. Pattern: horizontal push/brace.

timing_narrative:
**Preparation, exactly180s of targets.** The complete base occupies720s standard or420s compressed. P1 is40s:10s reminder in personal bays, then groups of five at10/20/30s; each10s action is4individual steps×2s+2s settle or the specified quiet-standing cycle. P1 requires20s before repeating that same short pattern; the earliest same-athlete P1→P2 stationary gap is40s. P2 is140s:20s gathering/route confirmation and three-athlete waves20/40/60/80/100s. Short start15s active+20s return; short walk18s+20s, last return138s. Stationary10s/no return. Same-lane20s releases can overlap an ordinary return: a walker’s18–38s return and next runner’s35–55s return overlap3s. Two same-direction returners require verified spacing/no catch-up, dedicated paths and no merge; if unavailable, delay/omit. Select stationary P2 independently without inventing its main-running evidence.

**Counted E0 orientation.** Main-relative0–120s includes transfer, instruction, selected markers and return/queue checks; a stationary athlete may return from P2 to its inspected personal bay here. Five waves of three start120/210/300/390/480s. Long walk45s active/marker/exit plus40s full return; short walk20s+20s; stationary orientation10s/no travel. The longest return ends565s.565–660s is feedback, route/intent/readiness selection and staging inside the setup period. Walking observes walking/conduct; it is not a screening run.

**Main E1.** Standard D rounds start main-relative660s and1170s; cap1 removes the second. Standard L uses one walking/stationary follow-up at660s. Compressed D uses660s once; compressed L has zero E1 after E0. Releases at offsets0,30,…420s cycle the three lanes; the same lane is reused every90s. Long run uses upper allowances5s build+5s rhythm+12s gradual runoff+3s exit=25s, then40s return. They are neither required split times nor speed targets for either3/10 or4/10. Long walk45s+40s is the longest85s complete action/return; short start15s+20s, short walk20s+20s, stationary10s/no return. The maximum85s clears before the next90s same-lane release. Return speed is never forced to meet that plan.

For two standard D rounds, same-athlete recovery after action and return is445s on a long run,425s on a long walk,475s on short acceleration and470s on short walking; stationary recovery500s. Required main recovery is90s traveling or60s stationary. Last standard D long-run return42:35, long-walk return42:55; last compressed D long-run return29:05, long-walk29:25. Remaining main time is feedback/water/strength setup, never another effort. Full-return E0→E1 gaps are checked per athlete. Stationary learners never consume a central staging/return interval; they remain in their visible personal bays.

**Five separate strength roles.** Standard45–51 knee,51–57 hip,57–63 push,63–69 pull,69–75 brace; each360s includes90s setup and five-person groups starting90/165/240s. Compressed35–39 knee,39–43 hip,43–47 push,47–51 pull,51–55 brace; each240s includes60s setup and groups60/120/180s. One set per role. Longest bouts: knee25s, unloaded hip21s, familiar DB hip26s including10s handling, push17s, both-side supported row52s, heel taps26s; breathing40s then15s quiet recovery. Shorter actual-history caps change repetitions only, never handling/tempo/rest.

The familiar DB route’s five inspected stations permit simultaneous familiar sets with two coaches observing2/3; it is not the paired first-DB teaching model. Hip group reset20s occurs after all active handling/sets clear. Compact maximum26+20=46s inside the60s group pitch; final compact hip set ends206s, allowing34s for feedback/transition. Standard pitch75s leaves more time. The longest compact row ends232s and breathing recovery235s in240s. Preserve90s after the loaded hip and60s for other familiar strength roles; each athlete’s fixed next-role start leaves more than that. Actual longer setup or unsuitable pair/space/coverage selects a compatible unloaded set or defers the role, not rushed loading.

Same35m corridor,2→4/10 build then relaxed4/10,25s active allowance+40s full return,90s recovery. Its FIRST modest increase requires actual repeatable prior2→3/3 long running and current runoff fit; no prior successful4/10 run is required. RETAINED modest work instead uses actual repeatable same-route2→4/4 and current response/runoff fit, without reconstructing an older3/10 record. One emerging attempt is not repeatability. **Independent P2 choice.** Every age may select one independently eligible short start (D only,5+10m,15s+20s return,easy2→3/10), short walk (15m,18s+20s,2/10), stationary basic march (4steps total,2each side×2s+2s settle,10s/no return,2/10), or quiet standing (2settle+2comfortable hold+6reset,10s/no return,minimal effort). P2 recovery60s. P1 is basic marching with the same10s action or quiet standing, but20s short-rehearsal recovery. P2 never uses the new4/10 effort or earns a full-route result.

**Stationary main choices.** Personal-bay E0 is one10s quiet-standing orientation,60s recovery and zero corridor travel. E1 basic march4steps total/twoeach side×2s+2s settle or quiet standing2+2+6s: every ageD2standard/1compressed,L1standard/0compressed or cap1,60s recovery, no travel/return. The assigned coach directly observes the personal bay in the reserved slot; no central staging is added. Comfortable support exchange is independently required for marching; quiet standing supplies none. No appropriate task means defer.

**Knee and hip history holds.** One bodyweight knee and one bodyweight hip set: D3/4/4 orL2/3/3 across9–11/12–14/15–18, only against actual compatible counts. Each explicit1/2/3-repetition cap uses min(reference,cap). Knee3s lower/1pause/1stand+5s setup; hip3s back/1stand+5s setup;60s recovery,at least5 good reps in reserve. Same actual pair/load/range;3s lower/1s stand,4s pickup+4s set-down+2s clear,90s recovery,at least5 good reps in reserve. Ten suitable DBs/five fitting elevated parking stations and direct two-coach observation of familiar independent sets are required. Record actual kg per DB/total and support height. No first loaded instruction or shorter familiar handling inferred from oneOR06 lesson. A more recent actual unloaded hip record retains bodyweight; returning to older DBs would be a separate change. Unavailable resources select deliberate unloading before pickup or defer, never an added replacement set after a fault.

**Supporting dose levels and replacements.** The default push/row/heel-tap tables below are the reference. To preserve a more recent low set on any day, use the explicit low support level: push1×2 age9–11 or1×3 ages12–14/15–18,2s down/1s up+5s setup; row1×2each side,4s per rep+10s side change+10s handling; heel tap1×1each side,4s each+10s setup; all60s recovery and familiar owned mechanics/load. A recorded still-smaller actual dose or unsuitability may reduce/defer it; no restoration follows from aD label.

Supported breathing replaces S5 for every age/mode:1×4comfortable breaths,nominal2s in/3s out,noholds orforceddepth,20s setup/exit=40s total then15s quiet recovery; calves/heels supported,bilateralreach,noheelpull/hiplift,fiveverifiedsupports. When preserving the low support level, use itsL1×3 even onD. Each needs independent support/grip/body-line or breathing readiness and replaces one role without awarding the replaced competency.

age_scaling_policy.equal_dose_reason: Short low-effort preparation is not age-based overload. Explicit equal doses across ages are deliberate; task skill, body size, comfortable range and current readiness decide the variant.
age_scaling_policy.readiness_independent_of_age: Experienced younger athletes may use qualified familiar actions; unfamiliar older athletes use instruction. Age never grants flight, rapid descent, floor support, loaded patterns or cue response.

layout_and_timing_assumptions.layout: Three columns of five distinct 3 m × 3 m personal bays: 15 independent working spaces. Five athletes share a lane assignment, never an overlapping crawl corridor.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.additional_space: Unobstructed peripheral coach circulation/access/egress and separately verified start, runoff and return corridors are additional to the 9 m × 15 m bay rectangle. The marked rectangle is not the total facility footprint.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.travel: Standing paths remain in personal bays. Short forward passes are at most 1.6 m; backward/lateral spans 1 m or less except 1.5 m carioca. Individually check full hand-walk/plank footprint before use.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.orientation: All bays face one end. Complete a pass and stop before ordinary walking return within that same bay. No crossing between athletes or concurrent opposite-direction traffic inside a bay.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.coaches: Familiar shared practice: one coach scans A/B and one scans B/C with clear oblique views. Three-wave teaching/checks: both coaches watch one active lane and split five athletes 2/3; other lanes stand. Clear views of all active feet/trunks are required.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.wave_handover: The active lane finishes standing, then the next lane starts on cue. The 2-second change (3 seconds for floor teaching) is a cue change, not relocation. Athletes stay in their own bays.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.equipment: Flat markers, bottles outside active rectangles, clean dry nonslip surface. No partner support, unstable props or unverified anchor is assumed.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.setup_before_clock: Mark/inspect space before class. Readiness/restriction information must be available. First demonstration includes stop cue and immediate comfort check. Unknown restrictions or inability to follow safe directions require individual resolution, never assumed clearance.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.clock_definition: Row time = demonstration + waves × individual execution envelope + explicit wave handovers + reset/transition. The individual envelope includes stated steps, pauses and returns. Shared practice means separate bays, not 15 times one athlete dose.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.tempo_rule: Execution envelopes are estimates for the stated variant, not speed commands. If safe learning/movement needs longer, use contingency, remove optional work or revise the booking. Never rush to validate arithmetic.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.bay_to_target_transition: Base ends at 12:00 full or 7:00 compact with athletes standing in bays. Reserve exactly 180 seconds for exactly two parent-owned target tasks. The parent exemplar defines the split and charges bay-to-start gathering, demonstrations, observed holds, rehearsal, exit and return within those 180 seconds. Use the parent-defined allocation; do not double-charge gathering or hide it before the base ends.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.physical_validation_status: UNVERIFIED: measured space, body fit, sightlines, surface, shared-floor schedule and target corridors have not been observed. Arithmetic does not certify physical feasibility.

teaching_and_competency_policy.full_familiar: Sixteen ordered slots with reminder demonstrations only. SP-11/SP-12 explicitly repeat mastered A-March because exact B/C identities are unverified.
teaching_and_competency_policy.compact_familiar: Eleven slots in original relative order. Omit SP-04, SP-10, SP-11, SP-12, SP-14. Retain floor purpose through the declared stationary-bear modification; hinge and squat remain last.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_full: Eleven recognizable slots in 12 minutes. Easy march replaces jog; optional crossing/flight/B/C complexity is omitted; lunges lose rotation/depth; floor flow becomes knees-down rock-backs; descent is slow; basic march/foot-roll precede observed hinge and partial squat-to-stand. After the easy raise, all actions are demonstrated and observed in three five-athlete waves.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_compact: Same eleven recognizable slots in 7 minutes. Basic walking/stepping/foot-roll can follow the coach in separate bays. Lunge, floor, slow drop, hinge and partial squat remain serialized in three observed five-athlete waves. One hinge and one squat cycle are readiness observations; qualification belongs to subsequent instructional work.
deferred_complexity: Traveling bear crawl and new complete plank/downward-dog flow
Full toe/ankle contact and overhead squat-to-stand range when unavailable
teaching_and_competency_policy.what_deferred_means: Practice the simpler named component in its original place; log performed variant and unfilled demand. Teach additional complexity in a relevant later instructional module. Do not silently pass it, substitute a generic unrelated warm-up or add teaching outside the clock.
teaching_and_competency_policy.partial_competency: Existing evidence can support a familiar variation, independently of age. Preparation completion does not unlock a main family: no-flight lowering is not landing, marching is not running, rock-back is not tumbling, and no throw/cue gate is tested here.
teaching_and_competency_policy.correction_limit: Use visible contingency for actual slower movement or brief corrective repeat and record time/dose/contacts. If essential teaching remains incomplete, mark profile/session REVISE and use the 12-minute instructional base or a justified booking adjustment. Never consume the reserved target time or speed up movement.
teaching_and_competency_policy.optional_reduction_order: For familiar full, remove SP-12 then SP-11, then SP-04/SP-10/SP-14 as readiness/purpose permits. Record omissions and revised clock. Compact/OR already omit these; beyond contingency, further necessary omissions require explicit review rather than an unqualified complete-base claim.

flight_not_qualified_overlay.application: For otherwise familiar athletes whose flight is unqualified, independent of age. This can accompany an independently qualified throw-only main branch, but does not itself authorize throwing or a cue.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-01: Easy march in place for the same 60 seconds full or 50 seconds compact; no flight.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-08: Retain a separately qualified no-flight rapid descent. If unlearned, slow drop squat to stick: 3 × 8-second envelopes, each 2 s lower + 2 s hold + 1 s stand + 3 s reset; no travel. Record changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-10: Omit four A-Skip hop landings; freed time is recovery, not another drill.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-13: Eight alternating no-flight foot-roll actions, four each side: 8 × 2 s + 4 s standing reset = 20 seconds; no travel. Log changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-14: Omit six bilateral pogo landing events; no substitute jump.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.accounting: Subtract omitted flight events and record actual time/contacts. Reduced-impact preparation grants no JUMP-T, REACT-T, throwing, early-release or go/no-go qualification.

stop_rules: Cease for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, loss of balance or inability to follow the stop cue; coach checks readiness.

records.name: Backpedal
records.purpose: Rehearse controlled backward travel and orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: A related backpedal-to-sprint identity is not this slow preparation task.

records.setup: Face the same end of the room. Mark 1 m behind the start; two short backward steps reach it, then two forward walking steps return. No turn or crossing.
cues: Short steps under you; look forward.
Check the clear space behind you before moving.
common_errors: Long reaching steps and backward lean.
stop_rules: Stop for obstacle, balance loss or pain; use ordinary walking return only when clear.

competency_rule.observe: Controls both backward steps and forward return with balance and stop-cue response.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Lateral shuffle
records.purpose: Access lateral movement with organized feet and controlled orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: This low-intent short shuffle is not reactive cutting.

records.setup: Start centered. Step-close without crossing for 1 m right and 1 m left back to start. Repeat only for the familiar dose.
cues: Stay facing forward; step then close.
Own the stop.
common_errors: Reaching past the bay or racing the return.
stop_rules: Stop if feet collide, boundary control fails or discomfort appears.

records.name: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog (ordered slot)
records.purpose: Prepare shoulder/wrist support, trunk control, hip movement and floor transitions with low fatigue.

verified_local_names: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog
Inchworm to World’s Greatest Stretch (related legacy flow)
card_mapping_status.limit: Exact composite not established. Stationary limb unloads explicitly replace traveling bear crawl for 15-bay delivery. Knees-down rock-backs are a declared partial-purpose regression, not an exact approved composite. The proposed stationary substitution is specifically four separately mastered single-limb lifts with full replants, not an unspecified weight shift or contralateral crawl.

records.setup: One athlete per dry nonslip 3 m × 3 m bay. Entire floor footprint fits before use. No shared slow-crawl lane or following crawler. Coach checks hand/knee comfort before support. Familiar bear support uses one limb at a time: left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot. A lift means the whole selected hand or foot briefly clears the floor by about 1–2 cm; it is not merely a weight shift. Fully replant and settle before the next limb.
cues: Hands comfortable; breathe with controlled trunk.
Quiet unhurried transitions; soft knees in downward dog.
Keep the trunk quiet; lift one contact only, then fully replant before the next.
Do not lift opposite hand and foot together.
common_errors: Forced straight knees or shoulder range.
Starting the next lift before the previous contact is fully replanted.
Rotating or sagging the trunk to clear the limb.
stop_rules: Stop for wrist/shoulder pain, slipping, trunk-control loss or inadequate footprint.
Use contingency or record incomplete rather than rushing floor entry.

Omit the familiar bear-lift component if any single-limb lift/replant has not already been mastered; use the entire named instructional floor profile and its coaching clock, or record incomplete purpose. No new bear-lift teaching is assumed inside the familiar reminder.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable actual support and floor entry/exit. Rock-back does not pass plank/bear or tumbling support. For familiar bear lifts, each selected contact clears briefly, fully replants, and the trunk remains quiet before the next lift.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Squat-to-stand with overhead reach — concluding check
records.purpose: Observe knee/hip/trunk organization through a comfortable sequence.

card_mapping_status.limit: Source 62 is review state. Familiar prescription follows candidate variant sequential-bilateral-reach-squat-to-stand: standing hinge/contact, comfortable squat, one controlled overhead reach per assigned side, stand/reset. Assigned order is left then right. Current exact dose/profile eligibility remains unverified. The OR thigh-supported partial version remains an explicitly different modification pending variant review.

records.setup: Same three five-athlete observation waves. Comfortable stance/reachable contact points; no forced toe touch or depth. Coaches see feet and trunk. Familiar source-linked sequence assigns LEFT reach and return, then RIGHT reach and return while the opposite hand maintains its comfortable toe/ankle contact; stand only after both reaches. Each reach stays in controlled comfortable range.
cues: Use comfortable range and a stable foot.
Reach without forced rib flare; stand smoothly.
Left reach and return, right reach and return, then stand; do not skip a side.
common_errors: Counting one reach as completion of the familiar sequential-bilateral cycle.
stop_rules: Stop for pain or uncontrolled balance/trunk; use declared partial sequence if comfortable. Longer teaching uses contingency or records incomplete.

competency_rule.observe: Observe actual sequence, foot pressure and control; not a loaded squat or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

workload_and_tumbling_interface.purpose: Finish warm and organized, not tired. Effort about 2/10 and conversational; this is not overload or conditioning.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.full_flight: Four unilateral A-Skip hop landings and six bilateral pogo landing events are explicitly prescribed in the familiar full profile. Timed easy jog and ankling also carry impact; their actual flight/contact detail is recorded instead of fabricated.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.compact_flight: A-Skip/pogo are omitted, but easy jog still has impact and ankling actual contacts remain in the record. Compressed is not automatically impact-free.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.or01_flight: No intentional flight in the first-visit profiles; no landing gate is thereby passed.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.upper_body: Familiar floor work includes a 4-second high plank, brief bear-position support/unloads and downward-dog access. Count wrist/shoulder/trunk demand alongside throwing, pressing, bracing and separate tumbling. Rock-back support is still support.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.tumbling: The separate 30-minute tumbling/Body Control allocation remains unprescribed here. Share actual comfort, support/impact exposure and observations with its coach. Its later load and staffing remain unverified.

reviewable_modifications.change: Easy jog in place and shortened bay-contained travel replace starting-distance layout.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Keep purpose with no crossing or long queue travel.

reviewable_modifications.change: Stationary bear-position limb unloads replace traveling bear crawl in the familiar composite.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Five sequential slow crawlers per lane cannot be treated as simultaneous overlapping athletes.
reviewable_modifications.alternative_arithmetic: At 32 seconds per athlete, five serial waves in three parallel lanes require at least 160 seconds of work before demo/clearance, versus 32 seconds with separate bays: 128 seconds extra. Adding that to the complete full clock exceeds 720 seconds without another explicit change.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: Purpose-preserving proposal; exact composite and facility delivery remain unapproved.

reviewable_modifications.change: B/C ordered slots perform and record only mastered A-March; compact/OR omit them.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Do not invent an unverified B-march, hip-opening march or C-skip.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: B/C identity/delivery remains unresolved; short A-March profile also needs review.

reviewable_modifications.change: Familiar concluding squat-to-stand now uses four full or two compact complete 8-second LEFT-then-RIGHT reach cycles. Compact hinge remains two reps; OR01 compact remains one observed hinge and one partial squat cycle.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Preserve both source-assigned reaches, safe control and ordered three-wave observation within 720/420 seconds. This explicitly reduces the philosophy full starting dose of five to four; compact squat count changes from three ambiguous cycles to two complete cycles. The philosophy permits scaled repetitions.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: Coach-review adaptation of repetition count and delivery, not publication or operational approval. Brief readiness observations do not pass competence; finish required evidence in instructional work.

reviewable_modifications.change: First-visit flow, reach, descent and rhythm use explicitly simpler/no-flight components.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Teach recognizable components honestly instead of pretending reminder demos teach every complex action.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: If actual essential instruction exceeds contingency, mark REVISE and use longer instructional base or another justified booking change.

validation.arithmetic_status: PASS: 16 ordered records; three explicit age bands; four doses/profile clocks; individual segment sums; group demo/work/wave/transition sums; contiguous 720/420-second bases; concluding hinge/squat order; exactly 180 seconds reserved for two target tasks.
unresolved: Measured floor footprint, body fit, sightlines and separate target corridors
Exact published card/variant/delivery eligibility and live facility approval
Observed timing with 15 actual athletes and unfamiliar transitions
Separate tumbling and whole-day recovery budget

validation.count_accounting_status: PASS: all 192 age/profile dose objects have explicit primary count units; included numeric doses reconcile through segment primary-unit contributions; bilateral landings retain event/foot distinction; null unknown contact counts remain null; override routes resolve explicit dose/rest/profile references or explicit zero-dose omission.

counting_conventions.primary_repetitions: Always interpret reps_total with count_unit and count_definition. Mixed flow constituents, side counts, foot contacts and timed segments are not interchangeable.
counting_conventions.segment_repetitions: Each execution segment has its own count_unit. Its duration remains repetitions × seconds_each. Primary count contributions convert the segment counts to the record primary unit; complete cycles remain the accepted unit.
counting_conventions.SP-09_and_fallback_normalization: A-March primary counts are now individual steps: 8 familiar (4 each side) or 4 OR (2 each side). Bilateral cycle counts are explicit secondary metadata; actual movement/time unchanged.
counting_conventions.SP-13_correction: Familiar full/compact is 16 individual ankling task contacts, eight each foot; OR01 full/compact is four individual foot-roll/replace actions, two each foot. No execution duration or physical dose changed.
counting_conventions.contact_rule: Landing events and per-foot landing contacts are separate. Timed jogging/actual ankling flight count stays null when not predetermined, never zero by default.

standard_D.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation

standard_D.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.
